content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"title\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"revisionId\": \"1b0d9b5d65\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:00:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:41:00Z\", \"text\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\nSheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "title": "Q4 investor update - send list", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list", "revisionId": "1b0d9b5d65", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:41:00Z", "text": "Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Ultimately, though, we don’t feel Harmony Games is the right fit for us at this stage. The content and market risk around scaling a new puzzle IP in the current environment feels higher than we’re comfortable with. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There\\u2019s a clear rhythm to how you\\u2019re executing.\\n\\u2022 We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you\\u2019re building toward true scalability.\\n\\u2022 There\\u2019s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2\\u20133 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t\\u2019s clear you\\u2019re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.\\nWhat\\u2019s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We\\u2019d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.\\n\\nWe also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. We\\u2019d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.\\n\\n\\nThis was a tough call. Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
Use the Slack tools (mcp__hg__slack_*) read-only. Do NOT post anything. HarmonyGames started a bridge round on Sep 3, 2025.

Read the full history of private channel #bridge-pitch (C096HFA5Z8W) with oldest=1756857600 and latest=1759302000. Use mcp__hg__slack_read_channel with response_format concise and paginate by cursor until done. Read thread replies with mcp__hg__slack_read_thread for any message that has replies.

Also search with mcp__hg__slack_search_public_and_private, after=1756857600, for each of these terms and read the relevant hits and threads, including DMs: "TestFlight", "testflight", "Play internal", "internal test", "tester", "pass", "passed", "reached out", "IH", "Matthew", "intro".

Report exhaustively for each investor firm, angel or organization:
- outreach about the bridge by us (Leonard, Fred, Robert, Arthur, IH/Ibrahim, Matthew, an advisor, Griffin), with date
- calls or meetings, with date
- passes or declines: exact quote, date, and whether the no was told to us directly, told to Griffin or an advisor, or is only an advisor's opinion
- whether the conversation is about investment or about publishing, co-dev, RFP or service
- build access per platform: who was added to TestFlight (iOS) and/or the Google Play internal track (Android), by whom (Arthur tracks adds), and when. Flag public-link-only sends, adds that were requested but not done, and adds on only one platform.

Also report any messages about the angels Kevin Lin, Mike Fischer, Demetri Detsaridis, Anton Bernstein or Paul Heydon committing or signing. Quote text and give ts/date for every claim. Final answer is a concise text report, not a file.

A background agent, "Summarize bridge investor email threads" (ac88739da4aa4fad5), is running. Do not duplicate it. Its output is at /tmp/claude-0/-app/3702e8c7-d560-4a49-923f-d3a3bc1ee228/tasks/ac88739da4aa4fad5.output.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- read_channel returns newest messages first. Paginate with next_cursor.
- Concise format shows thread_ts on thread parents, which marks messages to read with read_thread.
- User IDs:
  - EMPLOYEE_0038 = Leonard (CEO).
  - EMPLOYEE_0016 = probably Robert (Leonard: "the 'discussing' Robert heard via Applovin").
  - EMPLOYEE_0025 = probably Arthur (handles Google Play adds; also the "AI powered vs driven" remarks).

- Rough ts by date: Sep 17 ≈ 1758067200; Sep 18 ≈ 1758153600; Sep 22 ≈ 1758499200; Sep 23 ≈ 1758585600.

Page 1 (Sep 23–28):
- **Speedrun (a16z).** Leonard expects a rejection; no actual no received yet.
  - 1759085462: "I started to see people announcing their acceptance to speedrun..."

- **TapNation (game acquisition, i.e. publishing).**
  - 1758829572 (Sep 25): trying to schedule with "their game acquisition guys"; slots are 2am–6:30am.
  - 1758829538: "pinged [USERNAME_0458]"
  - 1758829656: Leonard booked an earlier LA flight for this meeting.
- **Play Ventures.**
  - Leonard emailed them Sep 3 (1758671806: "I emailed them back on Sept 3rd").
  - They never answered us (1758671737). Advisors [USERNAME_32018], Matthew and [PERSON_NAME_6550] did not ping them (1758671857).

import json,base64,sys,re
def walk(p):
    out=[]
    mt=p.get('mimeType','')
    d=p.get('body',{}).get('data')
    if d and mt.startswith('text/plain'):
        out.append(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(d+'==').decode('utf-8','replace'))
    for c in p.get('parts',[]) or []:
        out+=walk(c)
    if not out and d and mt.startswith('text/html'):
        t=base64.urlsafe_b64decode(d+'==').decode('utf-8','replace')
        out.append(re.sub('<[^>]+>',' ',t))
    return out
raw=open(sys.argv[1]).read()
d=json.loads(raw)
if 'result' in d and isinstance(d['result'],str): d=json.loads(d['result'])
msgs=d.get('messages',[d])
for m in msgs:
    h={x['name']:x['value'] for x in m['payload'].get('headers',[])}
    print('=====',m['id'][-25:],h.get('Date'),'\nFrom:',h.get('From'),'\nTo:',h.get('To'),'\nCc:',h.get('Cc'),'\nSubj:',h.get('Subject'))
    body='\n'.join(walk(m['payload']))
    # trim quoted
    cut=re.split(r'\nOn .{5,120}wrote:|\n>|-----Original|________________',body)[0]
    print(cut.strip()[:3000])
EOF

Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1757542625.945119\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I fed some additional datapoints to it\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757542614.893449\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"but again it has all the context\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757542601.626599\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"this is more chatgpt less me lol\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757542591.718649\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Progress summary \\u2014 Harmony Games Engine and traction\\n*Where the engine is today*\\n Harmony Games Engine is our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, content scheduling, economy tuning, analytics, and rapid creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build. We now port the stack into a new title in about 4 months at production quality, so a small team can learn faster and reuse success.\\n*Engine progression*\\n\\u2022 *Phase 1 (complete):* AI as assistant. Standardized live service infrastructure, level gen prototypes, physics-based 3D puzzle layer, boosters, leaderboards, quests, calendars, season pass. Goal was to harden the backbone.\\n\\u2022 *Phase 2 (in flight):* AI as junior designer. Automated level generation with constraints, difficulty scoring, authorable event tooling, experiment harness, and self-serve tools for designers. Live service personalization and faster iteration loops. Current status in Zombie Match: service integration ~60% complete with trophy path, leaderboards, quests, daily gift, teams online or in final integration. Creative pipeline from concept to first testable video in about 2 hours.\\n\\u2022 *Next (12 months):* Data-driven designer. Use live player data and reinforcement learning to adapt difficulty, rewards, and pacing. Move service execution toward \\u201cautopilot\\u201d with embedded analytics optimizing events across titles with human guidance.\\n*Traction and revenue*\\n\\u2022 *Domino Delights (live in small markets):*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Avg daily playtime: *~30 minutes*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Avg DAU over last 6 months: *~600*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 ARPDAU: *~$0.10*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Earlier retention reads landed below our scale bar (D7 in mid-teens, ~35% of D1), which capped LTV against CPI. We are not scaling this title. Domino Delights validated the engine\\u2019s content pipeline, physics, boosters, event systems, storefront, and offer framework. The game is now being positioned with a publisher while we reuse the stack on a better core.\\n\\u2022 *Zombie Match 3D (alpha, UK iOS tests):*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Early signals at minimal polish: *~34% D1*, *~23 min day-0 playtime*, *~$4.50 CPI* (small n)\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Live service integration ~60% complete, with remaining features on a short horizon\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Next 4\\u20136 weeks: expand to *500+ levels*, complete polish/VFX, and scale tests to *2\\u20133k* users for stable reads\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Gates to proceed: *\\u226545% D1*, *\\u226545% D7/D1*, *\\u2264$3.50 CPI* in UK iOS. We scale only if the data clears these bars.\\n*Why this matters*\\n The engine lets us compress concept-to-beta cycles, cut net-new code, and operate multiple shots on goal with a lean team. Domino Delights proved the platform. Zombie Match applies it to a distinct Match & Slash core aimed at Western audiences. The bridge focuses on finishing Phase 2 capabilities and driving Zombie Match from alpha into beta and soft launch with disciplined, data-led gates.\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757542591.229869\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"and this is progress summary\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757542207.076209\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"so I don\\u2019t know where it\\u2019s not me but chatgpt anymore lol\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757542186.868679\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"but pitch deck narrative was done by me first then chatgpt then me again\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757542160.122029\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"this is summary of out pitch deck narrative -> chatgpt -> me editing and making modifications\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757542054.939119\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"so the next one is biz summary: Harmony Games is an AI-driven mobile studio building the next breakout in puzzle-RPG. Founded in 2023, we raised a $3M seed led by GRIFFIN GAMING PARTNERS, a multi-billion dollar gaming-focused fund, alongside world-class advisors such as [PERSON_NAME_0090] and Matthew Collins, and assembled a senior, 17-person distributed team across the U.S., Europe, and South America. Our mission is simple: take many high-quality shots on goal, move fast, and scale only when the data says we\\u2019ve earned it.\\n\\nAt the center is Harmony Games Engine\\u2014our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, event scheduling (the \\u201clive service\\u201d layer), economy tuning, analytics, and creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build; now we can port the stack into a new title in ~4 months with production quality. The result is fewer one-off builds, faster iteration, and a small team that learns cheaper than traditional studios.\\n\\nOur first franchise with a break-through potential is Zombie Match 3D, introducing a new \\u201cMatch & Slash\\u201d subgenre: fast 3D matching where every match becomes a weapon, layered with items, upgrades, bosses, and horde modes. The game is live in early tests (alpha) with a growing content slate and service layer. Early UK iOS signals on minimal polish: ~34% day-one retention and ~25 minutes first-day playtime with only 100 levels and minimal polish. Over the next 4\\u20136 weeks we\\u2019ll expand to 500+ levels, add more polish/VFX, and scale tests to 2\\u20133k users. Go/No-Go gates are explicit: \\u226545% day-one retention, \\u226545% day-seven-to-day-one retention ratio, and \\u2264$3.50 CPI in UK iOS. We scale only if we clear the gates. If not, we\\u2019ll pivot to our next title\\n\\nOn the platform roadmap, we\\u2019re evolving AI from \\u201cassistant\\u201d to \\u201cjunior designer\\u201d toward a data-driven designer that adapts difficulty, rewards, and pacing from live player data. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. {"ok": true, "messages": [{"ts": "1759288987.503349", "type": "message", "text": "We got the expected rejection letter from A16Z - I think it’s very well-written response. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Leonard,

Done. The bridge-round send list (as of end of day Tue Sep 30 PT) is in my Q4 2025 investor update folder as "Q4 update - send list", and I've shared it with you: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nexW5wUL0FpnbnIZhkL7wnvxFXGrVdBs7SdeOl2O2gc/edit

Counts by group:
- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel (Anton Bernstein, $25K. His SAFE was reissued at 25 and the DocuSign Completed notice came in Sep 26)
- In talks: 7 firms (a16z, NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu Ventures, GFR Fund, HOMA, Brightwater Games Fund) and 1 angel (Paul Heydon, $50K. He says he signed, but there's no DocuSign Completed notice yet, so he isn't counted as a new investor)
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels
- Keep warm: 3 firms (LVP, Hiro Capital, Sciplay), 0 angels

Total: 24 firms and 2 angels. Everyone else from the 2025 list stays off, as you asked.

Build access for the firms in talks: T-Accelerate and Dentsu have iOS and Android. The other five have none, per Arthur's tester log.

On the Existing Investor Update card I added New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm checklists. I also created follow-up cards in To Do for everyone in talks or awaiting reply, with three exceptions:
- Dentsu and Makers have no card because they already have meetings on my calendar (Oct 1 and Oct 8).
- NCsoft already had a card ("F/up with Anel after the engine deep dive"), so I commented there instead.

A few calls you may want to check on Monday:
- a16z is in talks. The speedrun decision doesn't count as their answer on the bridge.
- The Sep 29 Turkish VC call isn't included because it was never on my calendar.

Fred

content.text:
The send list, the Trello updates and the reply to Leonard are all done, ahead of Monday's review (Oct 6).

**Send list.** I made a Google Sheet called "Q4 update - send list", as the folder's README asks. It's in your Q4 2025 investor update folder and shared with Leonard so he can edit it. It counts everything up to end of day Sep 30 Pacific. Each row has the group, amount, build access and the evidence I used.

| Group | Firms | Angels |
|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1: Anton Bernstein, $25K (his signed SAFE came through Sep 26, reissued at $25K) |
| In talks | 7: a16z, NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, GFR Fund, HOMA, Brightwater Games Fund | 1: Paul Heydon, $50K |
| Awaiting reply | 14 | 0 |
| Keep warm | 3: London Venture Partners, Hiro Capital, Sciplay | 0 |

Only T-Accelerate and Dentsu have access to the internal build (iOS and Android), based on Arthur's tester log in Linear. The other five firms in talks have none.

**Trello.** The Existing Investor Update card now has four checklists: New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm. The Keep warm one didn't exist yet, so I created it as Leonard asked in his Sep 14 comment. I added 19 "F/up with …" cards to To Do. Three people don't get a new card:
- Dentsu and Makers already have meetings on your calendar (Oct 1 and Oct 8).
- NCsoft already had a To Do card about Anel, so I commented on that instead.

**Reply to Leonard.** I replied on his thread with these counts and the sheet link. It went to Leonard only; Robert and Arthur weren't copied.

These calls could reasonably go either way, so they're worth a look on Monday:
- **Paul Heydon** says he signed, but there's no DocuSign "Completed" notice. Under Leonard's rule that means he's In talks, not a new investor.
- **a16z** is In talks. Their speedrun rejection doesn't count as an answer on the bridge.
- **Sciplay** passed by phone to Robert on Sep 30, so they're in Keep warm.
- The **Sep 29 Turkish VC call** is left off because it was never on your calendar.
- **Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital and General Catalyst** are in Awaiting reply based only on Leonard's Sep 12 Slack note that IH contacted them. I found no replies.
- **Treo VC** is in Awaiting reply: they messaged first and we sent the deck.
- **Initial Capital** is in Awaiting reply: they said they won't lead but might write a small check.

The two helpers I started for the email and Slack review both crashed without results, so I read those sources myself. I could only see your mailbox, not Leonard's, so a reply sent only to him wouldn't show up here.
